healthcare_exposure.selectivity: Selected from a highly competitive applicant pool (admission letter received 2026-04, before April 15 deadline)
healthcare_exposure.track: MEDscienceTECH Foundations — biomedical engineering + computer science + clinical medicine
healthcare_exposure.description: Completed June 22-26, 2026. Five-day program at Harvard Medical School. Key activities: (1) Diagnosed two simulated patients — Maggie (herniated disk, X-ray) and Linda (bladder/spine cancer, PET scan + X-ray). (2) Day 2: Used Roboflow to train a computer vision model on 200 labeled images to detect spine tumors ('orange balls'), then connected it via Python API to a robotic arm to remove tumors from a model spine in a 10-minute simulated OR under time pressure. (3) Day 3: Justin played the anesthesiologist in a 30-minute live OR drill on Linda — performed intubation (laryngoscope, ETT, Ambu bag), made real medication decisions under pressure (chose ketamine + epinephrine for emergency only + rocuronium), monitored vitals throughout. (4) Day 4: Used ChatGPT/LLM to diagnose orthopedic cases (osteomyelitis). (5) Day 5: Team built 'Nerve-1' — an AI computer vision surgical robot for glioblastoma (GBM) brain cancer removal. Justin handled financial Q&A and operated the live AI demo during the shark-tank pitch to 4 investors. Note: the Roboflow CV model was trained on 200 images with varied lighting conditions and struggled during the live demo under different lighting — Justin's team acknowledged the limitation honestly.
healthcare_exposure.why_it_matters: Materially stronger for applications than initially framed. For McMaster Q2A (healthcare technology evaluation): Justin has specific, technical biodesign experience — trained a CV model from scratch, integrated it via API, observed its failure mode under real conditions, and discussed how to improve it with investors. That is a 7/7 answer, not a 5/7. For Waterloo AIF: Nerve-1 is directly CS-relevant (Roboflow, Python API, CV model training, robotics integration, prototype-to-pitch). The anesthesiologist role adds clinical specificity that almost no applicant pool peer will have: intubation, medication decisions, 30-minute live OR under pressure. For Queen's PSE: the team engineering experience and clinical immersion both feed the personal narrative.
healthcare_exposure.notes: Program completed June 22-26, 2026. Journal written June 23 (detailed, 5-day). Platform note: 'Kepler AI surgical robotic platform' was never the actual tool — the correct description is Roboflow CV model + Python API + robotic arm (Day 2 spine project) and Nerve-1 (Day 5 team pitch). Application essay (data/justin/Harvard MEDScience.docx) framed Justin as 'Calm Analyst & Team Specialist' — consistent with his anesthesiologist role (careful under pressure, monitors systematically) and his honest acknowledgment of the model's failure mode during the demo.

The Roboflow CV model failure during the demo (lighting variation, 200-image training set) is exactly the kind of specific, honest reflection McMaster's rubric rewards at the top end. Journal written June 23. This is exactly the profile McMaster BHSc supplementary readers look for.
